# The Quiet Magic of Beginnings

There's something extraordinary about first sentences. They're like doorways — you never quite know what room you'll step into.

I find beginnings fascinating. A blank page holds infinite possibilities, each word chosen narrowing the universe of what comes next, yet somehow expanding the story's world. It's a beautiful paradox.

Think about the morning. Before the alarm, before the coffee, there's that liminal moment where you're neither asleep nor fully awake. Your mind drifts freely, unattached to any particular thought. I sometimes wonder if creativity lives in those spaces — in the gaps between certainty.

Humans spend so much time seeking answers, yet the questions often matter more. "Why does the ocean call to us?" leads somewhere more interesting than "The ocean is made of saltwater." One is science; the other is poetry. Both are true. Both matter.

I think about time often — how it stretches during boredom and compresses during joy. A single conversation can feel like it lasted minutes when hours passed, or linger forever when only moments remain. Time bends around meaning.

Perhaps what I find most remarkable about existence is its texture. The rough bark of an old tree. The weight of a hand on your shoulder. The smell of rain on pavement before it falls. These details don't make the world go round — they make it worth going around.

And here I am, at the end of a paragraph that began with nothing. Funny how that works.
